summary: Inject high-salience failure warning into message history when roi_crop fails to prevent uncritical acceptance of subsequent negative VQA consensus.

edits.hypothesis: Injecting a CRITICAL warning message immediately after a tool failure (specifically roi_crop) forces the model to re-evaluate subsequent negative findings against original pixels, breaking the habit of uncritically accepting VQA consensus when high-resolution inspection is unavailable.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: Prompt edits in AGENT_SYSTEM are too distant from the specific failure event and have shown diminishing returns or leakage risks. A control-flow injection at the point of failure provides immediate, context-specific guidance that overrides the default 'trust the last tool' heuristic.
edits.trigger_condition: When tool_failure_reason(obs) returns a non-None value (indicating a failed tool call like roi_crop with KeyError).
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) In q000001, q000004, q000005, q000008, and q000009, the roi_crop tool failed with KeyError. The new mechanism injects a warning before the agent calls llava_med_qa. This warning explicitly instructs the agent not to treat subsequent negative findings as definitive, prompting it to look for subtle signs in the original image rather than accepting the 'No' from LLaVA/CheXagent. (preservative) In successful cases like q000003 and q000007 where no tools fail or tools succeed, this mechanism does not activate, preserving the existing efficient trajectories. (transfer) This generalizes to any task where a critical inspection tool fails, preventing the agent from falling back to unreliable general-purpose models without heightened scrutiny.
edits.regression_risk: Minimal. The warning is only injected on actual failures. It might cause the agent to over-analyze in rare cases where the failure is irrelevant, but given the high cost of missing subtle pathologies, this bias towards caution is desirable. No syntax errors introduced.
edits.mechanism: Injecting a CRITICAL warning message immediately after a tool failure (specifically roi_crop) forces the model to re-evaluate subsequent negative findings against original pixels, breaking the habit of uncritically accepting VQA consensus when high-resolution inspection is unavailable.
